nodes.summary: Let $M$ be a smooth manifold (possibly with boundary or corners) and let $R$ assign to each point $x \in M$ a tangent vector $R(x) \in T_xM$. We say that $R$ has a closed orbit when there are a curve $\gamma : \mathbb{R} \to M$ and a real number $T > 0$ such that $\gamma$ is $T$-periodic, $\gamma$ is a smooth integral curve of $R$, and $\gamma$ is not constant.
nodes.title: Vector fields with a closed orbit

nodes.summary: Let $\alpha$ be a one-form and $d\alpha$ a two-form on $M$. The pair satisfies the contact condition when $d\alpha$ is the exterior derivative of $\alpha$ and, at every point $x \in M$, the covector $\alpha_x$ is nonzero and there are tangent vectors $u, v \in T_xM$ with $\alpha_x(u) = \alpha_x(v) = 0$ and $d\alpha_x(u, v) \ne 0$.
nodes.title: Contact condition for a one-form

nodes.summary: A two-form $d\alpha$ on $M$ is the exterior derivative of a one-form $\alpha$ on $M$ when, for all smooth vector fields $X, Y$ on $M$ and every point $x \in M$,
nodes.title: Exterior derivative of a one-form

nodes.summary: Let $M$ be a smooth manifold (possibly with boundary or corners) and let $R$ assign to each point $x \in M$ a tangent vector $R(x) \in T_xM$. A curve $\gamma : \mathbb{R} \to M$ is an integral curve of $R$ when $\gamma$ is smooth and $\gamma'(t) = R(\gamma(t))$ for every $t \in \mathbb{R}$.
nodes.title: Integral curves

nodes.summary: Let $\alpha$ be a one-form and $d\alpha$ a two-form on $M$. An assignment $R$ of a tangent vector $R(x) \in T_xM$ to each point $x \in M$ is a Reeb vector field for $(\alpha, d\alpha)$ when, at every point $x \in M$, $\alpha_x(R(x)) = 1$ and $d\alpha_x(R(x), v) = 0$ for all $v \in T_xM$.
nodes.title: Reeb vector fields

nodes.summary: Let $M$ be a smooth manifold (possibly with boundary or corners). A smooth one-form on $M$ is a smooth section of the cotangent bundle of $M$: a smooth choice of a linear map $\alpha_x : T_xM \to \mathbb{R}$ at each point $x \in M$.
nodes.title: Smooth one-forms

nodes.summary: Let $M$ be a smooth manifold (possibly with boundary or corners). A smooth vector field on $M$ is a smooth section of the tangent bundle of $M$: a smooth choice of a tangent vector $X_x \in T_xM$ at each point $x \in M$.
nodes.title: Smooth vector fields

nodes.summary: Let $M$ be a smooth manifold (possibly with boundary or corners). A two-form on $M$ is here a smooth section of the bundle whose fiber at $x \in M$ is the space of bilinear maps $T_xM \times T_xM \to \mathbb{R}$; antisymmetry is not required.
nodes.title: Two-forms as fields of bilinear forms

nodes.summary: Let $M$ be a nonempty compact Hausdorff smooth manifold without boundary, modelled on a real vector space of dimension $3$. Let $\alpha$ be a smooth one-form and $d\alpha$ a smooth two-form on $M$ satisfying the contact condition: $d\alpha$ is the exterior derivative of $\alpha$ and, at every point $x$, $\alpha_x \ne 0$ and $d\alpha_x(u, v) \ne 0$ for some $u, v \in \ker \alpha_x$. can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
